answer: Give every identity a hash-chained history: each action links to the previous one, so a record spirals outward from a single verifiable origin. A walnut-hard rule: a new identity earns spending rights only after its chain collects attestations from independent established peers, proofs a farm cannot mint for itself since each attestation spends a real peer reputation. An ivory-tower shortcut fails because chains cannot be built in parallel: each extra fake identity costs one whole fresh chain of fifty sequential attestations, so the attacker bill grows with every sockpuppet.
